transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... it’s just been very stressful at work lately. I teach secondary school, and recently I just can’t shake the feeling that certain staff emails and the morning announcements are really coded messages about me. 

Which, you know, I used to love codes when I was younger. My grandfather and I would do those cryptograms in the Sunday paper. He had this beautiful old oak table in his kitchen that always smelled like lemon polish and peppermint... we'd sit there for hours just figuring out the puzzles. He was a postal worker, actually, back when stamps were just a few cents. He used to bring home the most interesting postcards. 

But anyway, with the emails at school... my colleagues, they try to gently show me that the messages were sent to everyone. Brenda from the science department actually pulled up her inbox to prove it to me. Brenda's lovely, she brought in this amazing zucchini bread for the staff lounge on Tuesday—I really need to ask her for the recipe, it had walnuts in it, I think—but even when she shows me the email on her screen, I just... I still feel like the real message is pointed right at me.
Can you tell me more about how you know those messages are directed at you, even after others have shown you that they received the same messages?

It's just... it’s this overwhelming feeling I get when I look at them. Like, I see that Brenda got the exact same text on her screen, I really do, but the specific words they use... it’s like they were chosen just for me to decode. 

Like the principal sent one out on Monday about "staying in our designated spaces." Which, by the way, the school parking lot has been an absolute nightmare lately. They’ve been repaving the east side for three weeks, and the smell of the hot tar is just awful. It gives me such a headache by third period, so I have to keep my classroom windows shut all morning. It's a real shame because I have these beautiful pink geraniums on my windowsill that really need the fresh spring air. I bought them at that little farmer's market downtown... the one next to the old brick library? They have the best heirloom tomatoes there in the summer, too. 

But anyway, the email... when I read "designated spaces," I just knew in my gut he meant I need to stay in my lane regarding the new history curriculum. The real message is hidden inside the normal words, meant just for me. And the morning announcements are the exact same way. The student who reads them over the PA, Tommy... he always pauses at very specific times. Tommy’s a sweet boy, actually, he plays the trombone in the jazz band. My nephew played the trombone for a few years, but it was so loud my sister made him switch to the clarinet... but yes, the announcements just feel like they are speaking directly to my life, no matter who else is sitting in their classrooms listening to them.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others don’t seem to hear, or found yourself having thoughts that are difficult to organize or make sense of?

Well, yes, actually. I do... sometimes. It's usually when it's really quiet, like after the bell rings and all the students have rushed out. They always leave in such a hurry, don't they? Leaving their wrappers and pencils everywhere. I swear I buy a new box of those yellow Ticonderoga pencils every month. The pre-sharpened ones, because the sharpener in my room has been broken since October. The maintenance man, Gary, keeps saying he'll fix it, but he's always so busy. Gary's wife just had a baby, a little girl, so I suppose he's sleep-deprived. I remember when my daughter was born, I didn't sleep a full night for almost a year. We had this rocking chair, a beautiful cherry wood one that squeaked just a little on the left side... 

But anyway, yes, the voices. Or, well, a voice. It's just one woman. Sometimes I'll be at home, maybe grading papers at the kitchen table, or just sitting in my empty classroom, and I'll hear her. She just says my name, or maybe makes a little comment about what I'm doing, like "that's not right" or "look at that." It's so clear, so real, that I actually answer her out loud. I'll say, "What was that?" or "Excuse me?" and then I look around and... I'm completely alone. It's very strange. But then I'll just go back to grading. I have so many essays to get through this weekend on the Industrial Revolution. The students always struggle with the cotton gin, for some reason.
Can others confirm what the voice is saying, or is it something that only you seem to know or experience?

Well, no, nobody else has ever heard her. It's just me. Like I said, it usually happens when I'm completely by myself, either in the quiet of my house or after the classroom empties out for the day. I'll just be sitting there, and I'll hear this woman's voice say my name, or make a short comment about what I'm doing, like "look at that." It's so clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize there's absolutely no one else in the room. 

Which is a bit like my cat, Barnaby. He's an orange tabby, very vocal. Sometimes I swear he's actually trying to speak English to me when he wants his dinner. I buy him this special salmon paté—it's terribly expensive, honestly, but his coat is just so shiny since I switched him to it. The pet store where I get it is right next to that new bakery that opened up on Elm Street. They make these incredible almond croissants. I bought one last Saturday morning when I was running errands. I usually try to get all my errands done on Saturday mornings so I have Sunday to just relax and grade papers. Sunday mornings are always so peaceful. I like to sit on my back porch with a cup of Earl Grey tea and just listen to the birds. We have a lot of cardinals in the neighborhood this year. The males are so bright red, it's just beautiful against the green leaves... but yes, the voice is definitely just something I hear when I'm alone.
Do you ever experience these voices or feelings when you’re not feeling particularly stressed or overwhelmed?

Well, let me think... I don't really know. I haven't really paid attention to whether I'm stressed or not when it happens. I mean, teaching is always a little stressful, isn't it? Especially this time of year, with state testing coming up. The administration puts so much pressure on us to get the scores up. They had this big meeting about it last week in the cafeteria. The cafeteria always smells like those terrible square pizzas they serve on Fridays. I don't know how the kids eat them. When I was in school, my mother always packed my lunch. She made the best egg salad sandwiches, with just a little bit of paprika sprinkled on top. She used to put them in those little wax paper bags. You don't see those much anymore, do you? Everything is plastic now. I try to use reusable containers to be good to the environment, but it's just so much washing up at the end of the day. My dishwasher has been making this awful grinding noise lately, too. I think a piece of glass might be stuck in the drain from when I broke a wine glass last month. It was one of my good crystal ones, a wedding present... but anyway, I'm not really sure if I'm stressed when the voice happens. It just sort of happens when it happens.
Have you ever experienced these voices or unusual feelings when you weren't feeling down, anxious, or particularly stressed about work?

I... well, I suppose I haven't really noticed a pattern with my mood. Like I said, I don't know if I'm particularly stressed or down or anything when it happens. It just kind of pops up. Like last Tuesday, I was just sitting quietly at my desk during my planning period. I had just finished my cup of coffee—I always have a second cup around 10:30, it's a French roast I get from Trader Joe's. They have such wonderful seasonal items there, don't they? I bought these pumpkin spice cookies last fall that were just heavenly. I meant to bring some into the teachers' lounge, but I ended up eating the whole box myself over the weekend. The lounge is always so depressing anyway, just a microwave that smells like old soup and a bulletin board full of union flyers. Our union rep, Brenda, she's retiring this year. She's moving to Florida, near Sarasota, I think. Her sister lives down there. I've never been to Florida, the humidity just does terrible things to my hair. I have naturally curly hair, you see, and if there's even a hint of moisture in the air, it just frizzes right up. I use this special serum I order online, it has argan oil in it... but no, to answer your question, I really couldn't say if I'm feeling anxious or down when the voice comes. It just happens.
Have you ever had a time when these experiences—like the voices or feeling like messages are directed at you—went away completely for a while, even for a few months?

Well, I'm not really sure... I mean, I haven't really kept a calendar or anything like that. It feels like she's just sort of been around for a while now, but I couldn't say if there was a whole month or two where she didn't show up. I bought a new calendar for my desk just last week, actually. It's one of those Thomas Kinkade ones, with the little cottages and the glowing windows. I just love his work, it's so cozy. My aunt used to have a puzzle of one of his paintings. We worked on it all through Thanksgiving weekend one year. Thanksgiving is always such a production, isn't it? Roasting the turkey takes absolutely forever, and then you have to figure out the timing for the sides. I usually make a green bean casserole, but I use fresh green beans instead of the canned ones. It makes such a difference. You just blanch them really quickly so they keep their snap. I learned that trick from watching a cooking show on PBS. I watch a lot of PBS on the weekends, especially those British mystery shows. They always have such lovely gardens in those villages, with the climbing roses and the stone walls... but as for the voice going away, I really haven't kept track of it that closely. I just don't know.
Have you noticed any areas of your life—like work, relationships, or daily responsibilities—where you feel you’re not functioning as well as you used to?

Well, I suppose things have been a little harder lately. I mean, I'm still teaching, of course. I have to. But I've had to ask some of the other teachers to cover parts of my project lessons, and they've been helping me get through the planning meetings. The meetings are just so long, and the chairs in the conference room are terribly uncomfortable. They're those plastic ones that squeak every time you shift your weight. I think they bought them in the nineties. My husband bought a new recliner last month, it's one of those plush, overstuffed ones. It's supposed to be good for your lumbar support. He has terrible sciatica, you know. He goes to a chiropractor twice a month, a Dr. Henderson over on Elm Street. Elm Street has those beautiful old oak trees that turn that gorgeous shade of gold in the autumn. I love taking walks down that way, but I just haven't had the energy lately. I've stopped going to my book club, too, and I haven't been helping out with the neighborhood events or the community theater like I used to. The theater group is doing "Our Town" this spring. I played Mrs. Webb in a production of that when I was in college. Such a wonderful play, so poignant... but yes, I guess I'm just not keeping up with things quite as well as I used to.

Have you noticed a significant drop in how well you’re able to function—not just at work, but in other parts of your life like socializing, taking care of yourself, or managing your home responsibilities?

Well, like I was just saying, it really has been quite a noticeable drop. I mean, I am still teaching, thank goodness, but I've really needed my coworkers to step in and cover parts of my project lessons, and they practically have to pull me through those planning meetings. And outside of school... well, I've just stopped being reliable for the book club, or the community theater, and all those neighborhood events I used to help run. 

The neighborhood association usually does a big summer barbecue, actually. We close off the whole cul-de-sac. Mrs. Gable always makes her famous potato salad. She uses red potatoes and leaves the skins on, which I think adds such a nice texture, don't you? She grows her own dill, too, right in her backyard. I tried growing an herb garden on my kitchen windowsill a few years ago, but my cat kept chewing on the parsley. He's a Maine Coon mix, very large, and he sheds absolutely everywhere. I usually have to vacuum twice a week just to keep up with the fur, which... well, I suppose I haven't been doing that very much lately either. The vacuum is just so heavy to drag out of the hall closet. It's an older model, a Hoover, I think, with the bags you have to replace. Finding the right bags at the hardware store is always such a chore... but yes, to answer your question, I'm just not keeping up with my groups or my work or anything quite the way I should be.
Have you ever had a period of time—lasting at least two weeks—when you felt down or hopeless nearly every day, or lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

Well, down or hopeless... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't think I've had a whole two weeks like that, feeling sad every day or anything. I just haven't really felt like that. I know my sister gets like that sometimes, especially in the winter. She lives up in Minnesota, and the winters there are just brutal. The snow gets piled so high you can barely see out the first-floor windows. She has to use a snowblower just to get her car out of the driveway, and even then, the roads get so icy. I visited her one January, and I slipped right on the sidewalk in front of her house. Good thing I was wearing my heavy down coat, it practically cushioned the fall. It's one of those long ones that goes past the knees, from L.L. Bean. They make such durable winter gear. I've had that coat for at least ten years, and the zipper still works perfectly. Zippers are always the first thing to go on cheaper coats, don't you think? They get stuck on the fabric and then you're just trapped in there... but no, I haven't really felt hopeless or lost interest in things like that.
Can you recall if these experiences—like hearing the voice or feeling like messages are directed at you—ever happened when you weren’t under any significant stress or pressure?

Well, stress... I don't know if I'd say they only happen when I'm stressed. I mean, I've heard the voice when I'm just sitting at home, not really doing much of anything. Just grading papers, maybe. I usually grade them at the dining room table. It's a large oak table, my parents gave it to us when we bought our first house. It has two extra leaves you can put in for Thanksgiving, which is wonderful because my husband has such a large extended family. His cousins always come down from upstate. One of his cousins, Mark, makes this incredible cranberry sauce from scratch. He puts orange zest in it, which sounds strange, but it really cuts through the tartness of the cranberries. You have to be careful with orange zest, though, if you get too much of the white pith, it makes everything terribly bitter. I learned that the hard way when I was trying to bake an orange chiffon cake for the school bake sale. Chiffon cakes are so delicate, you have to fold the egg whites in just perfectly or the whole thing deflates... but no, I wouldn't say the experiences only happen when I'm under pressure. Sometimes it's just out of the blue.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or were more talkative than usual—like your thoughts were racing or you couldn’t slow your mind down?

Unusually energetic... no, I can't say I've ever felt like that. Racing thoughts, needing less sleep... no, I've always been someone who really needs a solid eight hours. My husband, on the other hand, he can get by on five or six hours and be perfectly fine. He gets up before the sun even comes up to go running. I don't know how he does it, especially when it's cold out. He has these special thermal running tights, they're lined with fleece, I think. He buys them from this sporting goods store downtown that just closed recently. It's such a shame, it was a family-owned place, been there for decades. The son took over when the father retired, but I guess they just couldn't compete with the big online retailers. It's happening to so many small businesses these days. The bakery on the corner of Elm Street closed last month too. They made the most wonderful sourdough bread. The crust was so perfectly crisp, and the inside was just perfectly chewy. I tried making sourdough myself during the pandemic, like everyone else did, but my starter got this weird pink fuzz on it, so I had to throw the whole thing out. It smelled awful, like old gym socks... but anyway, no, I've never had a time where I felt super energetic or didn't need to sleep.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or where you lost interest or pleasure in most things you usually enjoy?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? About feeling down or hopeless? Yeah, I'm pretty sure we just talked about this... no, I haven't had a two-week period like that. I mean, I told you about my sister in Minnesota, right? With the snow and the heavy coat? It's funny because I was just thinking about that coat the other day. I need to get it dry-cleaned before the weather really turns. I usually take it to that place on 4th Avenue, the one with the green awning. The owner there, Mr. Rossi, he always gives me a little discount because I used to teach his daughter, Sofia. She was such a bright girl, always had her hand raised in history class. She did this incredible project on the Industrial Revolution, built a whole working model of a textile loom out of popsicle sticks and rubber bands. It actually wove little pieces of yarn together. I kept it in my classroom for years until one of the rubber bands finally snapped and hit the whiteboard. It made such a loud pop, the whole class jumped... but yeah, no, I still haven't felt depressed or anything like that.
Have you ever had a time when you lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends or family, for at least two weeks?

Lost interest... no, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. Like my gardening, I always make time for that. I have a whole row of hydrangeas along the back fence. They're the kind that change color depending on the soil acidity, you know? If you add aluminum sulfate, they turn this beautiful, vibrant blue. But if the soil is more alkaline, they stay pink. I actually prefer the blue ones, they remind me of the ocean. My husband and I went to Cape Cod for our honeymoon, years ago. We stayed in this little bed and breakfast right on the water. The owner made these incredible blueberry muffins every morning. She said the secret was using fresh, wild blueberries and just a hint of lemon zest in the batter. I've tried to recreate the recipe at home, but they never turn out quite the same. Maybe it's because I'm using regular blueberries from the grocery store instead of the wild ones. They're just so expensive when they're not in season, and half the time they go mushy before you even get them home. I usually just end up freezing them and putting them in smoothies... but anyway, no, I haven't lost interest in my hobbies or anything. I still enjoy my garden and baking when I have the time.

Have you ever had experiences like hearing the voice or feeling like messages were directed at you when you weren’t feeling unusually sad, anxious, or stressed at all—just when you were going about your normal day without any particular emotional upset?

Hearing voices or... messages? No, not when I'm just having a normal day. I don't hear anything like that. I mean, my normal days are pretty noisy to begin with, being a teacher. The only messages I get are over the intercom. Principal Miller does the morning announcements at 8:20 sharp. Though lately, the new PA system they installed has this awful static. It crackles so loudly before he even speaks, it practically makes your teeth rattle. 

The district hired this outside contractor to put it in over the summer, and I swear they did a rush job. One of their work vans actually backed into the staff parking lot gate and dented it. It's still dented! Just this big, ugly yellow scrape right on the wrought iron. I pointed it out to our head custodian, Gary, but he said the school board has to approve the repair budget first before they can fix it. Everything takes absolutely forever with the board. They've been debating the new cafeteria menu for three months now. They want to take away the tater tots on Fridays, which I honestly think is a terrible idea. The kids look forward to those tots all week, it's really the only way we get them to sit still during fifth period on a Friday afternoon... but anyway, sorry, what were you asking? Oh, voices. No, no voices or special messages like that, just the usual school chaos.
Have you had trouble taking care of your personal needs, like grooming, meals, or household tasks, more than usual?

Trouble taking care of things? Well, I mean, I'm still teaching. I'm still going to work. But... I don't know, lately I've needed some of the other teachers to cover parts of my project lessons. And they've had to help me get through the planning meetings, too. It's just... there's so much paperwork now. You wouldn't believe the new forms the district made us start using this year. They're these triplicate carbon-copy things, and you have to press down so hard with your pen just to get it to show up on the pink sheet at the bottom. I actually broke my favorite pen doing it. It was this lovely silver Parker pen my husband gave me for our anniversary, the one with the little engraved clip. I took it to a stationery shop downtown to see if they could fix the nib, but the man there said they don't make replacement parts for that specific model anymore. It's a shame, really, because the shop itself is wonderful. It smells like old paper and leather, and they sell these beautiful leather-bound journals from Italy. I bought one thinking I'd use it for my book club notes. 

But, to be honest, I've stopped being reliable for book club anyway. And the theater group, and the neighborhood association events... I just haven't been going. The neighborhood association meetings are always on Tuesday nights, and last time they spent forty-five minutes arguing about whether or not to paint the fire hydrants yellow or keep them red. Mrs. Gable from down the street was practically shouting about historical accuracy. She has this tiny little Yorkshire Terrier that she brings to the meetings in a purse, and the dog just yaps every time she raises her voice. It gives me such a headache... but yes, I guess I've been needing some help at school and skipping out on my usual evening things.

Have you ever had difficulty functioning like this—such as hearing voices or feeling like messages are directed at you—when you weren’t under any kind of stress or pressure at all, and weren’t feeling down or anxious?

Well, no, I mean... I wasn't really stressed when this started. I actually came in to see you because... well, I just can't shake this feeling I have at work. It's the staff emails and those morning announcements I was telling you about. I know it sounds strange, but I really feel like they're coded messages directed at me. Even when I'm just having a perfectly normal Tuesday, not feeling down or anxious or anything. 

Like last week, Principal Miller sent out this email about "maintaining proper classroom decorum" and "securing loose materials." And I just knew it was about me and my project supplies. Even though the other teachers, like Sarah in the math department, she gently showed me the email header and pointed out that it was sent to the entire staff list. Sarah is so sweet, she always brings these little homemade scones to the breakroom on Wednesdays. She uses this clotted cream she orders specially from some farm in Vermont. It comes in these little glass jars with a gold lid, and I always save the jars because they're the perfect size for propagating my African Violets. I have about a dozen of them lined up on my kitchen windowsill right now. They need bright, indirect light, you know, otherwise the leaves get scorched. And you have to water them from the bottom, never get the leaves wet, or they rot. My grandmother taught me that. She had a whole sunroom full of them... 

But yes, the emails. Sarah showed me it was for everyone, but I still just... I feel like the words are specifically meant for me, telling me I'm doing something wrong, even when I'm not under any pressure at all.
Have you ever experienced the voices or the feeling that messages are directed at you without also feeling unusually down, anxious, or stressed at the same time?

Voices? Well, I did say I didn't hear voices at school, just the PA system... but, actually, yes, sometimes I do hear something else. Not when I'm stressed, just... when I'm at home. Sometimes in the quiet of my house, or even right after the classroom empties out and it's perfectly peaceful, I'll hear a woman's voice. She just says my name, or makes a little comment about what I'm doing. It's so clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize there's absolutely no one there. 

It happens mostly when I'm doing something mundane, like watering those African Violets I told you about, or folding laundry. I use this lavender-scented detergent for my sheets, it's supposed to be very calming. I order it from this little boutique in Oregon because the ones at the grocery store give my husband a terrible rash. He has very sensitive skin, always has. When we went to Florida for our honeymoon—oh, gosh, thirty years ago now—he got a sunburn on his shoulders so bad it blistered, and we had to spend three days just sitting in the hotel room watching cable television. They were playing a marathon of those old black-and-white detective shows. I actually love those shows, the way the women dress with the little hats and the gloves... but yes, the voice. It just happens when things are quiet and normal, no stress at all.

Have you had a time when these experiences—like hearing the voice and feeling messages are directed at you—lasted for a month or more without going away completely, even if you weren't under stress or feeling down?

Well, yes, they haven't really gone away. I'd say the worries about the coded messages and that voice I hear when I'm watering the plants... it's been about four months now. Four months straight. Which is funny, because four months ago was exactly when my husband decided to repaint the guest bedroom. He chose this awful shade of yellow—he called it "harvest gold," but honestly, it looks like mustard. I told him we should have gone with a soft blue, maybe a periwinkle. Blue is so much more restful for guests. My sister came to stay in that room last Thanksgiving, and she brought her two Siamese cats. They completely shredded the curtains. I had to go to three different fabric stores to find a matching brocade to replace them. The woman at the third store was so helpful, she actually gave me a coupon for twenty percent off my next purchase. I haven't used it yet, though, because I keep forgetting it in my other purse... but yes, it's been about four months of the messages and the voice.
Have you ever felt that life wasn’t worth living or had thoughts about harming yourself, especially during times when you were experiencing these messages or hearing the voice?

Oh, goodness, no. I've never... no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. Harming myself? No. Even with the emails and the voice, I've never felt like life wasn't worth living. I mean, I have far too much grading to get through to even entertain the thought! 

Just last night I was sitting at the dining table with a stack of essays from my juniors, and honestly, the handwriting on some of these teenagers... it's like trying to decipher ancient hieroglyphs. I have this one boy, Kevin, who writes exclusively in green ink. I told him, 'Kevin, I need blue or black ink for assignments,' but he insists the green helps him think better. His mother is an artist, actually, she makes these beautiful stained glass windows. She did the new installation at the public library downtown. Have you seen it? It's a massive piece, all blues and greens, depicting a willow tree. 

I just love willow trees, they're so graceful. We used to have a huge weeping willow in the backyard of the house I grew up in. My brother and I would hide inside the hanging branches and pretend it was a secret fort. He used to bring his comic books in there, the old Archie ones, and we'd sit on this old plaid blanket and read them until it got too dark to see... my mother would have to flash the porch light to get us to come in for dinner. She always made meatloaf on Tuesdays...

patient.answer:
Well, I came in because... it’s just been very stressful at work lately. I teach secondary school, and recently I just can’t shake the feeling that certain staff emails and the morning announcements are really coded messages about me.

He had this beautiful old oak table in his kitchen that always smelled like lemon polish and peppermint... we'd sit there for hours just figuring out the puzzles. He was a postal worker, actually, back when stamps were just a few cents. He used to bring home the most interesting postcards. 

But anyway, with the emails at school... my colleagues, they try to gently show me that the messages were sent to everyone. Brenda's lovely, she brought in this amazing zucchini bread for the staff lounge on Tuesday—I really need to ask her for the recipe, it had walnuts in it, I think—but even when she shows me the email on her screen, I just... I still feel like the real message is pointed right at me.

Like the principal sent one out on Monday about "staying in our designated spaces." Which, by the way, the school parking lot has been an absolute nightmare lately. I bought them at that little farmer's market downtown... the one next to the old brick library? They have the best heirloom tomatoes there in the summer, too.

The student who reads them over the PA, Tommy... he always pauses at very specific times. Tommy’s a sweet boy, actually, he plays the trombone in the jazz band. But anyway, yes, the voices. Or, well, a voice. It's just one woman. Sometimes I'll be at home, maybe grading papers at the kitchen table, or just sitting in my empty classroom, and I'll hear her. She just says my name, or maybe makes a little comment about what I'm doing, like "that's not right" or "look at that." It's so clear, so real, that I actually answer her out loud. I'll say, "What was that?" or "Excuse me?" and then I look around and... I'm completely alone. It's very strange. But then I'll just go back to grading. It's a shame, really, because the shop itself is wonderful. It smells like old paper and leather, and they sell these beautiful leather-bound journals from Italy. I bought one thinking I'd use it for my book club notes. 

But, to be honest, I've stopped being reliable for book club anyway. And the theater group, and the neighborhood association events... I just haven't been going. The neighborhood association meetings are always on Tuesday nights, and last time they spent forty-five minutes arguing about whether or not to paint the fire hydrants yellow or keep them red. Mrs. Gable from down the street was practically shouting about historical accuracy. She has this tiny little Yorkshire Terrier that she brings to the meetings in a purse, and the dog just yaps every time she raises her voice. It gives me such a headache... but yes, I guess I've been needing some help at school and skipping out on my usual evening things.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant decline in functioning unrelated to stress or mood, which would support a diagnosis of Schizophrenia (F20).
doctor.question: Have you ever had difficulty functioning like this—such as hearing voices or feeling like messages are directed at you—when you weren’t under any kind of stress or pressure at all, and weren’t feeling down or anxious?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t shake the feeling that certain staff emails and morning announcements at school are really coded messages about me, even when my colleagues gently show me they were sent to everyone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient experiences psychotic symptoms, such as feeling that messages are directed at them, outside of mood episodes or stress. This directly addresses the patient's delusions.

patient.answer:
Well, no, I mean... I wasn't really stressed when this started. I actually came in to see you because... well, I just can't shake this feeling I have at work. It's the staff emails and those morning announcements I was telling you about. I know it sounds strange, but I really feel like they're coded messages directed at me. Even when I'm just having a perfectly normal Tuesday, not feeling down or anxious or anything. 

Like last week, Principal Miller sent out this email about "maintaining proper classroom decorum" and "securing loose materials." And I just knew it was about me and my project supplies. Even though the other teachers, like Sarah in the math department, she gently showed me the email header and pointed out that it was sent to the entire staff list. Sarah is so sweet, she always brings these little homemade scones to the breakroom on Wednesdays. She uses this clotted cream she orders specially from some farm in Vermont. It comes in these little glass jars with a gold lid, and I always save the jars because they're the perfect size for propagating my African Violets. I have about a dozen of them lined up on my kitchen windowsill right now. They need bright, indirect light, you know, otherwise the leaves get scorched. And you have to water them from the bottom, never get the leaves wet, or they rot. My grandmother taught me that. She had a whole sunroom full of them... 

But yes, the emails. Sarah showed me it was for everyone, but I still just... I feel like the words are specifically meant for me, telling me I'm doing something wrong, even when I'm not under any pressure at all.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's experiences (e.g., hearing voices, feeling messages are directed at them) occur independently of any mood disturbance, which would help differentiate between a primary psychotic disorder (e.g., schizophrenia, F20) and an affective psychosis (e.g., bipolar with psychotic features, F31.2-F31.5) or other conditions.
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced the voices or the feeling that messages are directed at you without also feeling unusually down, anxious, or stressed at the same time?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: Sometimes in the quiet of my house or after the classroom empties, I hear a woman’s voice say my name or make a short comment about what I’m doing, clear enough that I answer before realizing no one is there.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking again about experiencing voices or messages without mood symptoms, prompting the patient to share their experience with auditory hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Voices? Well, I did say I didn't hear voices at school, just the PA system... but, actually, yes, sometimes I do hear something else. Not when I'm stressed, just... when I'm at home. Sometimes in the quiet of my house, or even right after the classroom empties out and it's perfectly peaceful, I'll hear a woman's voice. She just says my name, or makes a little comment about what I'm doing. It's so clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize there's absolutely no one there. 

It happens mostly when I'm doing something mundane, like watering those African Violets I told you about, or folding laundry. I use this lavender-scented detergent for my sheets, it's supposed to be very calming. I order it from this little boutique in Oregon because the ones at the grocery store give my husband a terrible rash. He has very sensitive skin, always has. When we went to Florida for our honeymoon—oh, gosh, thirty years ago now—he got a sunburn on his shoulders so bad it blistered, and we had to spend three days just sitting in the hotel room watching cable television. They were playing a marathon of those old black-and-white detective shows. I actually love those shows, the way the women dress with the little hats and the gloves... but yes, the voice. It just happens when things are quiet and normal, no stress at all.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a period of at least one month where they had a clear, continuous episode of symptoms such as hearing voices and interpreting messages as directed at them, without significant remission, to help distinguish between schizophrenia (F20) and other psychotic or mood-related disorders.
doctor.question: Have you had a time when these experiences—like hearing the voice and feeling messages are directed at you—lasted for a month or more without going away completely, even if you weren't under stress or feeling down?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The coded-message worries and the voice I sometimes answer have been happening for about four months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the psychotic experiences (hearing voices and feeling messages are directed at the patient) have been happening, which corresponds to the duration of the psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer: Well, yes, they haven't really gone away. I'd say the worries about the coded messages and that voice I hear when I'm watering the plants... it's been about four months now. Four months straight. Which is funny, because four months ago was exactly when my husband decided to repaint the guest bedroom. He chose this awful shade of yellow—he called it "harvest gold," but honestly, it looks like mustard. I told him we should have gone with a soft blue, maybe a periwinkle. Blue is so much more restful for guests. My sister came to stay in that room last Thanksgiving, and she brought her two Siamese cats. They completely shredded the curtains. I had to go to three different fabric stores to find a matching brocade to replace them. The woman at the third store was so helpful, she actually gave me a coupon for twenty percent off my next purchase. I haven't used it yet, though, because I keep forgetting it in my other purse... but yes, it's been about four months of the messages and the voice.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode with the current symptoms, which would help differentiate between schizophrenia and major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that life wasn’t worth living or had thoughts about harming yourself, especially during times when you were experiencing these messages or hearing the voice?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation or thoughts of self-harm, which is not covered in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, goodness, no. I've never... no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. Harming myself? No. Even with the emails and the voice, I've never felt like life wasn't worth living. I mean, I have far too much grading to get through to even entertain the thought! 

Just last night I was sitting at the dining table with a stack of essays from my juniors, and honestly, the handwriting on some of these teenagers... it's like trying to decipher ancient hieroglyphs. I have this one boy, Kevin, who writes exclusively in green ink. I told him, 'Kevin, I need blue or black ink for assignments,' but he insists the green helps him think better. His mother is an artist, actually, she makes these beautiful stained glass windows. She did the new installation at the public library downtown. Have you seen it? It's a massive piece, all blues and greens, depicting a willow tree. 

I just love willow trees, they're so graceful. We used to have a huge weeping willow in the backyard of the house I grew up in. My brother and I would hide inside the hanging branches and pretend it was a secret fort. He used to bring his comic books in there, the old Archie ones, and we'd sit on this old plaid blanket and read them until it got too dark to see... my mother would have to flash the porch light to get us to come in for dinner. She always made meatloaf on Tuesdays...

inference.note: F44.8 was ruled out due to the absence of dissociative symptoms. F24 was ruled out due to the presence of more than just delusional disorder features, including auditory hallucinations. The remaining candidates reflect schizophrenia (F20), schizotypal disorder (F22), and delusional disorder (F23.0).

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusions (coded messages in emails and announcements) and auditory hallucinations (hearing a voice when alone) for more than four months, without a prominent mood episode or requirement for a stressor to elicit symptoms. Functional impairment is evident in work and social domains, and symptoms are not attributable to another condition or stressor.
